headline: A US federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit claiming Sirius XM's algorithmic hiring tools discriminated against Black applicants.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: the full Law.com text supports the headline; the ruling date is not stated.
importance_line: What changed: a Detroit federal judge threw out a class action against Sirius XM Radio over algorithmic hiring, finding that many rejections and a zip-code proxy were not enough to prove discrimination. Job applicants and employers that use hiring algorithms are affected; the ruling is one decision in one case and may guide similar suits.
summary: Law.com reports that a federal judge in Detroit dismissed a class action accusing Sirius XM Radio, the US satellite radio company, of using algorithmic tools that discriminated against Black job applicants. The court found that many rejected applications, and zip code used as a proxy for race, were not enough to show race discrimination or disparate impact (unequal effect on a group) discrimination.
